title: Molecular-Level Understanding of the Influence of Ions and Water on HMGB1 Adsorption Induced by Surface Hydroxylation of Titanium Implants.
authors: Ranathunga, Dineli T S; Arteaga, Alexandra; Biguetti, Claudia C; Rodrigues, Danieli C; Nielsen, Steven O
journal: Langmuir : the ACS journal of surfaces and colloids
one_liner_zh: 该文用MD模拟研究HMGB1蛋白在钛植入体表面羟基化修饰下的吸附行为及离子/水的影响，属于蛋白质-无机表面互作而非TF-DNA体系，但MD方法可迁移至蛋白-DNA界面建模，故给予中档评分。
abstract: Due to its excellent chemical and mechanical properties, titanium has become the material of choice for orthopedic and dental implants to promote rehabilitation via bone anchorage and osseointegration. Titanium osseointegration is partially related to its capability to form a TiO(2) surface layer and its ability to interact with key endogenous proteins immediately upon implantation, establishing the first bone-biomaterial interface. Surgical trauma caused by implantation results in the release of high-mobility group box 1 (HMGB1) protein, which is a prototypic DAMP (damage-associated molecular pattern) with multiple roles in inflammation and tissue healing. To develop different surface strategies that improve the clinical outcome of titanium-based implants by controlling their biological activity, a molecular-scale understanding of HMGB1-surface interactions is desired. Here, we use molecular dynamics (MD) computer simulations to provide direct insight into the HMGB1 interactions and the possible molecular arrangements of HMGB1 on fully hydroxylated and nonhydroxylated rutile (110) TiO(2) surfaces. The results establish that HMGB1 is most likely to be adsorbed directly onto the surface regardless of surface hydroxylation, which is undesirable because it could affect its biological activity by causing structural changes to the protein. The hydroxylated TiO(2) surface shows a greater affinity for HMGB1 than the nonhydroxylated surface. The water layer on the nonhydroxylated TiO(2) surface prevents ions and the protein from directly contacting the surface. However, it was observed that if the ionic strength increases, the total number of ions adsorbed on the two surfaces increases and the protein's direct adsorption ability decreases. These findings will help to understand the HMGB1-TiO(2) interactions upon implantation as well as the development of different surface strategies by introducing ions or ionic materials to the titanium implant surface to modulate its interactions with HMGB1 to preserve biological function.
abstract_zh: 由于其优异的化学和机械性能，钛已成为骨科和牙科植入物的首选材料，通过骨锚定和骨整合促进康复。钛的骨整合部分归因于其形成TiO(2)表面层的能力，以及植入后立即与关键内源性蛋白相互作用的能力，从而建立首个骨-生物材料界面。植入引起的手术创伤导致高迁移率族蛋白B1（HMGB1）释放，这是一种典型的损伤相关分子模式（DAMP），在炎症和组织愈合中具有多重作用。为了通过控制生物活性来开发不同的表面策略，以改善钛基植入物的临床结果，需要对HMGB1-表面相互作用进行分子尺度的理解。在此，我们使用分子动力学（MD）计算机模拟，直接揭示HMGB1在完全羟基化和非羟基化金红石（110）TiO(2)表面上的相互作用及可能的分子排列。结果表明，无论表面羟基化程度如何，HMGB1最可能直接吸附在表面上，这并不理想，因为可能导致蛋白质结构变化而影响其生物活性。羟基化TiO(2)表面对HMGB1的亲和力高于非羟基化表面。非羟基化TiO(2)表面上的水层阻止离子和蛋白质直接接触表面。然而，观察到如果离子强度增加，两种表面上吸附的离子总数增加，而蛋白质的直接吸附能力降低。这些发现将有助于理解植入后HMGB1-TiO(2)相互作用，以及通过向钛植入物表面引入离子或离子材料来调节其与HMGB1的相互作用以保持生物功能的不同表面策略的开发。
